text:
marta: Heads up — running long-context eval (120k tokens) on the kvcache/paged-attn branch shows steady GPU memory growth instead of stable reuse. Repro: small chat model, batch size 1, continuous append of 2k tokens every iteration. After ~40k tokens memory climbs ~2 GB per 10k tokens and we eventually hit OOM on MI250.
omar: Can you paste the exact run command and the branch? Which model and quantization are you using?
marta: Model: rwood-small-7b (faux name), q4_0, branch: kvcache/paged-attn-fix2. Command:
```bash
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6
./serve --model rwood-small-7b --quant q4_0 --long-ctx 120000 --feed-loop 2k
```
I also enabled kvcache debug logs: `KV_DEBUG=1`.
omar: Thanks. Do you have profiler traces? nvprof or rocprof?
marta: Attached short perf excerpt (copied):
```
[H100] pagewalks/s: 1.15e6  evict_ops/s: 1.8e5  avg_pt_walk_ms: 0.9
[MI250] pagewalks/s: 2.32e6  evict_ops/s: 4.5e4  avg_pt_walk_ms: 1.5
[A100] pagewalks/s: 9.8e5   evict_ops/s: 2.0e5  avg_pt_walk_ms: 0.8
```
MI250 has ~2x pagewalks and much fewer evictions — looks like eviction isn't triggering correctly, causing PT shadow entries to pile up.
kai: That's consistent with a PT shadowing mismatch we saw. On MI we had an ordering issue where PT invalidate races with reuse window and the allocator didn't reclaim the shadow entry. Quick workaround: reduce reuse window and force more eager eviction. e.g.
```bash
export KV_REUSE_WINDOW=32   # (was 128)
export KV_EVICT_AGGRESSIVITY=1.2
```
Also try disabling soft-shadowing: `KV_SHADOWING=off` to see if it stabilizes.
deepa: I reproduced on MI250 with similar script. Additional counters from rocprof:
```
pt_walk_total: 2.4M
pt_ref_inc_no_reclaim: 1.9M
ghost_ptrs_detected: 8.7k
```
If ref_inc doesn't pair with a decrement we get leaks. On H100 I see matching inc/dec.
ben: I suspect the page-table decrement path (evict completion) isn't being called when the async evict callback races with a kernel restart. Adding an ordered completion fence in the evict path fixed a similar issue. I can push a small probe branch: `kvcache/pt-probe-fence` that toggles the ordering for testing.
omar: Also try forcing synchronous evict on MI for a short run to confirm: `KV_SYNC_EVICT=1`. It will hurt perf but confirm correctness.
marta: Quick test: set KV_SYNC_EVICT=1 + KV_REUSE_WINDOW=32 on MI250 — started the run, after 50k tokens memory plateaued (no further growth) for 10 minutes. Looks promising but throughput dropped ~18%.
deepa: Can you paste a log snippet where you still saw growth? I want to grep for `pt->refcount` and `evict-complete` lines.
marta: here's trimmed log around growth window:
```
[00:41:12] kvcache: alloc page id=0x3f2 ref++ -> 2
[00:41:12] kvcache: pt_walk start id=0x3f2
[00:41:12] kvcache: alloc page id=0x4a7 ref++ -> 1
[00:41:12] kvcache: evict queued id=0x3f2
[00:41:12] kvcache: (missing) evict-complete id=0x3f2  <-- expected
[00:41:13] kvcache: pt_walk end id=0x3f2
```
Note the missing evict-complete between queued and end in several spots.
ben: That's the signature. I'll instrument an extra `evict-complete` log in the branch and add a fence. Will drop the branch PR and link it here when ready.
deploy-bot: CI: kvcache/pt-probe-fence ran 3 smoketests — 2 passed, 1 flaky (long-ctx stress) — details: https://ci.internal/runs/9821
kai: If the probe fixes the race, we should consider making the evict completion synchronous only on architectures with non-coherent DMA ordering (or until we have an atomic refcount fix). Also add a small unit that simulates repeated reuse-window churn for >=100k tokens.
omar: For triage: (1) confirm reproducer, (2) run with KV_SYNC_EVICT=1 to prove mitigation, (3) try ben's probe branch, (4) measure throughput impact and roll a targeted fix.
marta: I'll run the full 120k token suite with ben's branch tomorrow on MI and H100 and post traces. For now sync-evict + smaller reuse-window is a safe mitigation for customers hitting long-context growth.
ben: PR incoming in ~30m with a small toggle and logs. If folks can smoke it on A100/H100/MI, ping me.
marta: great — thanks all. I'll update the incident doc if we verify a regression and coordinate a rollback plan for the Hosted fleet if needed. :thumbsup:
